description.narrative: Det huvudsakliga målet med projektet är att stärka kvinnors ledarskap och deltagande i det politiska livet. Det kommer att tillämpa FNs Gender Equality in Elected Office-metod för att få fler kvinnor valda på alla nivåer, inom alla beslutsfattande församlingar i Bosnien och Hercegovina. Projektet kommer att sikta på att öka kvinnors engagemang i det offentliga livet och stärka deras position i beslutsfattandet och försäkra att de har en realistisk och likvärdig chans som deras manliga motparter i de kommande allmänna valen (2018), och på längre sikt, de nästkommande lokala valen 2020. För att stärka kvinnors ledarskap och deltagande i det politiska livet kommer tvådelar strategier att användas - vertikalt genom att föreslå strukturella anpassningar för att få mera kvinnor i politiken samt horisontellt genom att nära nästa generations kvinnliga ledare genom skräddarsydda nätverks- och kapacitetsbyggande initiativ. Följande resultat förutses inom projektet: RESULTAT 1: Stärka kvinnors ledarskap RESULTAT 2: Främja politisk deltagande av kvinnor Projektet kommer att använda "ingångspunkter" och programmeringsmöjligheter för att öppna utrymmen för kvinnors ledarskap och stärka deras deltagande i det politiska livet. FNs kommer att ge samma stöd till alla utan några fördelar mot någon.

The main objective of the project is to strengthen women’s leadership and participation in political life. Guided by the strict observance of the highest standards of political neutrality, the project will apply the UNs Gender Equality in Elected Office approach to help secure an enabling environment for getting more women elected across board, in all spheres of decision-making in Bosnia and Herzegovina. It will look into enhancing the women’s engagement in public life and their position in the decision-making and ensure they are given a realistic and equal chance as their men counterparts in the forthcoming general elections (2018), and in the longer term, the next local elections in 2020 by advocacy for women’s equal rights and political participation. Strengthening women’s leadership and participation in political life will apply the two-pronged approach- vertically by proposing structural adjustments to accommodate greater numbers of women in politics, as well as horizontally by nourishing the next generation of women leaders in communities through tailored networking and capacity building initiatives. The following outputs are foreseen within this project: OUTPUT 1: Strengthening Women’s Leadership OUTPUT 2: Fostering Political Participation of Women The project will utilise the “entry points”, contextual enablers, and programming opportunities to open up spaces for women’s leadership and strengthening their participation in political life. UN support will be provided equally to all across the political spectrum with no favours towards anyone.

Theory of Change puts forth the big picture and delineates strategic thinking on how to make desirable change. It provides for a general direction since it makes connections between many different aspects of social life, which are influencing each other, often in a non-linear way. This project is designed having in mind a long term vision, while identifying medium term niches that pave the way for it. In doing so, it adopts a proven approach adjusting it to the BiH context, while pursuing series of activities incrementally. The long run progressive change of BiH society critically depends on activation of womens engagement and resources. High level of gender equality improves overall quality of life and contributes to the economic and democratic development of BiH. To that end, gender equality is seen not only as a human right issue, but also as a key development issue. Gender equality is taken as an essential precondition for redefining political and development agendas on the local and state levels. This is achieved by two different, but complementary set of activities: 1. Applying the Gender Equality in Elected Office: 6 Step Action Plan to ensure structural changes that provide an enabling environment, legislatively, institutionally and substantively, and 2. Empowerment of women locally to identify, strengthen and nourish the next generation of women leaders

description.narrative: Results achieved by the end of intervention were satisfactory, even the preset targets were not being met. Furthermore, the overall assessment is that the project led to some good and satisfactory results, but on the whole, the project has not had the leverage we thought it would had when we started. The project itself was prepared and initiated to start before the Parliamentary lections in 2018, however due to various reasons actual implementation started with a significant delay. Due to the complexity of the political situation and the need to avoid possible controversy and backlash against gender, it was necessary to consult with the UNDPs Department of Political Affairs in New York. One of the instructions from the UNDPs Department of Political Affairs included moderation during 100 days of electoral campaigning, which resulted in the cancellation of a media campaign. Therefore, continuation of the project also included regular consultations with relevant UN counterparts in Brussels and New York, which is to include screening of all concept notes on individual or groups of activities, which can be perceived as politically sensitive. These were significant delays in implementation of the project activities during the first year of implementation. Moreover, complex political situation marked by a highly negative preelection campaign and post election lack of forming the government(s) also influenced on implementation of project activities. The consultation process for composing the ToR for the Baseline Study took much longer than anticipated. COVID19 crisis took over attention and resources from other perceived priorities. The project, with its horizontal impact on communities, and vertical connection to institutions has had a potential for catalysing and bringing on positive social change, but also in educating population about transformative potential of gender equality, and the importance of having more women in decision making and leadership positions. The project facilitated the enhancement and reaffirmation of positive identity for women leaders. The Baseline Study, created in the beginning of the project was becoming a vital document for the Project. It was used by internal UNDP "gender" related projects, but also by an external actors active in the gender equality area
